title: Jurisdictional enforcement gate and KMS usage obligator
author: Aria Chen
description: Motivation: customers with strict data residency and key custody requirements asked for an enforcement primitive that guarantees request-level jurisdictional constraints are evaluated and enforced before any KMS operation or model selection occurs. This PR implements a lightweight Jurisdictional Enforcement Gate (JEG) middleware that integrates with RBAC v2 policy expressions, enforces a KMS Usage Obligator (declared by tenant policy), and strengthens audit continuity by signing per-request audit envelopes. Design summary: 1) Introduce a new policy predicate namespace 'jurisdiction:' in RBAC v2 (examples in docs) allowing rules like 'jurisdiction:region == eu-west-1 and kms:provider in (aws, gcp)'. 2) Add JEG middleware in the front proxy path that resolves request claims (tenant, region_hint, operator_scope) and short-circuits requests that violate jurisdictional or KMS obligations. 3) KMS Usage Obligator enforces that certain tenants/routes must use pinned KMS providers/regions; the gate will inject a required_kms context or reject the request with 403 when not satisfied. 4) Audit continuity: every enforced decision produces a signed audit envelope (ed25519 over canonicalized envelope) and a monotonic audit sequence number per-tenant, forwarded to the audit-forwarder with delivery guarantees; envelopes include the jurisdiction assertion and KMS choice. Migration & rollout: feature-flagged behind 'jrg-2025' with three modes: monitor-only (log violations), enforce-soft (reject but allow operator override), enforce-strict. Default rollout plan is monitor-only for two weeks, canary to 10% of tenants, then full enforcement after SOC review. Backwards compatibility: legacy RBAC policies still work; the gate ignores jurisdiction predicates if absent. Operational controls: metrics (jrg.violation_count, jrg.enforced_count), a new Prometheus alert for spike in violations, and an installer flag for private deployments to provide HSM/KMS integration credentials. Security & threat model: keys used to sign envelopes are stored in tenant-scoped sealed secrets or customer-managed HSM when available; ephemeral signing keys rotate daily and are attested via our KMS attestor component. References: ENG-2045 (Linear), SUP-7890 (support ticket), design doc link: docs/compliance/jurisdictional-enforcement.md. Why this is different: unlike earlier region-pin middleware, JEG ties RBAC predicates, KMS obligations, and signed audit envelopes together so enforcement and non-repudiation are co-located in the decision path.

release_notes: Adds Jurisdictional Enforcement Gate (feature-flagged), KMS Usage Obligator tied to RBAC v2 predicates, and signed per-request audit envelopes. Default mode is monitor-only. See docs/compliance/jurisdictional-enforcement.md for rollout and config.
security_considerations: Signing keys: tenants using customer-managed HSM will have keys provisioned via the KMS attestor; otherwise keys are generated and sealed per-tenant. Ensure installer sets 'installer.hsm.enabled' for on-prem. Enforced mode will return 403 for non-compliant requests and may impact integrations that rely on region-agnostic KMS use. Audit envelopes contain minimal PII (tenant id, request id, policy id, timestamp); payloads are base64-encoded to avoid transport mangling.
testing_summary: Unit tests: rbac predicate evaluation, kms obligator logic, envelope signing/verification. Integration tests: e2e scenarios for monitor/enforce-soft/enforce-strict across AWS/GCP KMS stubs. Canary run: 10% tenant canary for 48h produced 0 false positives in QA dataset. CI: added compliance pipeline job that exercises installer template with HSM enabled and checks audit-forwarder backpressure behavior.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (monitor-only): enable feature-flag 'jrg-2025' globally but in monitor-only for 14d. Phase 2 (canary): enable enforce-soft for 10% of tenants for 48h with ops oncall watching jrg.violation_count and jrg.audit_forwarder_failures. Phase 3 (enforce-strict): batch enable for remaining tenants after SOC signoff and postmortem review. rollback: disable flag or flip to monitor-only; installer provides jrg.rollback script to invalidate sequence allocator and resume previous behavior.
